newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker in heavy trading.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended weaker on Tuesday, after a sluggish session * TSE's 14 sub-groups were evenly split * 94.6 million shares traded for a value of C$1.15 billion
Toronto stocks ended slightly weaker on Tuesday along with modest U.S. losses as investors awaited direction from economic data later this week.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 1.43 points to close at 5147.12 in heavy turnover of 94.6 million shares valued at C$1.15 billion.

Declining stocks outpaced advances 502 to 394 with 297 issues ending flat. "I think everybody is sort of holding their breath to see what happens with the inflation data out of the United States," said John Kellett, vice president of equities for Royal Bank of Canada.
Kellett said Canadian equities did not get help from bonds, which ended mixed along with a weak U.S. market.
Debt markets were unsettled by remarks from Federal Reserve Board governor Janet Yellen who said that the U.S. economy has entered an inflationary danger zone.
Toronto's 14 sub-groups were evenly divided with the weak side led by golds and communications. The TSE's strongest gains were in banking, real estate and transportation.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Gibraltar Mines rose 1.30 to 7.60 on 2.1 million shares after Westmin Resources launched a C$307 million takeover bid.
Westmin led heavy traders, falling 1.25 to 6.25 on 4.4 million shares.
* In real estate, Trizec Corp jumped 0.85 to 11.35, a new 52-week high, after Horsham Corp unveiled a proposed merger with the property giant. Horsham gained 0.85 to 19.10.
* Micrologix Biotech Inc climbed 0.15 to 3.55 on 2.4 million shares after a large block trade.

* The gold sector was depressed by weak gold prices, but a few stocks shone today. Placer Dome Inc rose 0.10 to 32.10 after the gold miner said it expects a US$11 million gain from the sale of its stake in Gibraltar to Westmin.
